title: Robust Fano-like Antiresonances in Large-Area Au-coated Ag-Nanoisland Ensembles
authors: Valeria Nocerino, Francesca Di Carlo, Luca De Stefano, Principia Dardano, Carlo Forestiere
abstract: We investigate plasmonic resonances and Fano-like interference in Au-coated Ag nanoislands fabricated by solid-state dewetting followed by Au overgrowth. By combining electrostatic spectral analysis, full-wave simulations, and linear transmission spectroscopy, we show that the optical response is governed by hybridization between plasmonic modes supported by the Ag-island and the Au-coating. Increasing the Au-coating thickness red-shifts the low-energy resonance and transfers spectral weight from high-energy to low-energy resonances, while a pronounced anti-resonant dip remains nearly fixed. The eigenmode analysis identifies this dip as the signature of destructive interference between super-radiant and sub-radiant hybridized modes. These results establish coated bimetallic nanoislands as promising platforms for tunable Fano-like optical responses accessible through standard far-field spectroscopy, using a fabrication route that requires no lithographic patterning and is compatible with large-area, low-cost production.
summary: This work analyzes plasmonic resonances in Au-coated Ag nanoislands, demonstrating that their optical response exhibits robust Fano-like antiresonances. By simulating and measuring the effect of coating thickness, the authors show this system provides a simple, scalable platform for tuning these interference features using standard far-field spectroscopy.
main_problem: The study investigates robust Fano-like antiresonances in plasmonic systems using Au-coated Ag nanoisland ensembles, aiming to establish these structures as tunable platforms for optical response.
main_result: Increasing the Au-coating thickness shifts the low-energy resonance while leaving a pronounced anti-resonant dip nearly fixed, demonstrating tunability via simple fabrication methods.
method: The research combines electrostatic spectral analysis and full-wave electromagnetic simulations with experimental linear transmission spectroscopy measurements.
model_or_system: The physical system is Au-coated Ag nanoisland ensembles (bimetallic nanostructures). The theoretical model uses a boundary-integral equation approach solved in the quasi-electrostatic limit to analyze mode hybridization.
key_observables: Plasmonic resonances, Fano-like antiresonant dips, spectral weight transfer, and the electric dipole moment $p(	ilde{\omega})$.
important_parameters: Au-coating thickness ($t$), plasma frequency mismatch parameter ($\delta$), and geometry ratio ($t/r$).
main_assumptions: The analysis is performed within the quasi-electrostatic limit, neglecting retardation effects.
figures_summary: Figures schematically show the nanoisland structure with defined domains (island, coating, exterior) and illustrate spectral responses showing resonance shifts and fixed anti-resonant dips as a function of material parameters.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the general context of bimetallic plasmonics to developing the theoretical framework using boundary integrals. It then analyzes how key parameters like coating thickness and plasma mismatch ($\delta$) control the resulting Fano interference features, culminating in experimental validation.
why_interesting: While focused on classical electromagnetism (plasmonics), the concept of destructive quantum-like interference (Fano resonance) between hybridized modes is highly relevant to open quantum systems and cavity QED studies involving engineered dissipation channels.
